name: WebGPU in-browser inference is 2-5x slower than native GPU inference
symptom: The same model that runs at 30 tokens/sec on a native GPU may run at 6-15 tokens/sec in the browser via WebGPU, or 1-5 tokens/sec via WASM.
root_cause: Browser inference has multiple layers of overhead: the browser's sandboxed execution environment, WGSL shader compilation at runtime, lack of direct hardware access, and immature kernel libraries. WASM adds another layer of overhead with 128-bit SIMD vs 256-bit AVX2. The result is 2-5x slower than native GPU inference and 5-20x slower than native CPU inference.
workaround: Use WebGPU for zero-install web applications where convenience matters more than performance. For maximum performance, use native inference (llama.cpp, MLX, ONNX Runtime). Consider WebGPU for small models (1-7B) where the performance gap is less noticeable.
notes: The performance hierarchy for local inference: native GPU (CUDA/Metal) > native CPU (AVX2) > WebGPU > WASM. WebGPU is 2-5x slower than native GPU. WASM is 5-20x slower than native CPU. For a 7B model at 4-bit, native GPU might yield 50-100 tokens/sec, WebGPU 10-30 tokens/sec, WASM 2-10 tokens/sec. WebGPU is the right choice for web applications, not for maximum performance.
